[[File:YodaSoupBowlReplica.png|230px|thumb|A facsimile of the hearty soup eaten by Jedi Master Yoda on Dagobah]]
{{Quote|Eat, eat. Hot. Good food, hmm?|Yoda, while serving Luke Skywalker rootleaf stew|<ref name="ESB" />}}
'''Rootleaf stew''' was a favorite [[Foodstuff/Legends|meal]] of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] during his [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] on [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]]. It was a staple of his diet, supplemented by [[Yarum seed/Legends|yarum seeds]], [[Mushroom/Legends|mushroom]] spores, [[Galla seed/Legends|galla seeds]], and [[Sohli bark/Legends|sohli bark]]. Yoda prepared rootleaf stew the evening that he met [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].

In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> a facsimile of rootleaf stew was available to [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. It appeared to be made of a rich assortment of the [[Swamp/Legends|swamp]] [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] unique flora. However, it was in fact made from [[Fiberplast/Legends|fiberplast]].<ref name="TPoV">{{SWGTCG|set=The Price of Victory|swglink=Yoda soupbowl.png|cardname=Yoda Soup Bowl Replica}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In an unusual promotional campaign for the [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|''Empire Strikes Back'' radio dramatization]], National Public Radio hired [[Craig Claiborne]], a renowned chef and food critic, to create a version of rootleaf stew that could be made with ingredients originating from Earth&mdash;primarily lamb, spinach, parsley, onions, and many different spices. The recipe was published in newspapers and magazines across the United States.<ref name="Scranton">{{WebCite|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/scrantonian-tribune-star-wars-stew/113828012|text=Feed Young Jedis Yoda's Herb Stew |work= the Scrantonian-Tribune (archived at Newspapers.com)|date=1983-02-13|archivedate=20240123005920}}</ref><ref name="SWLH">{{WebCite|url=https://starwarslivinghistory.com/2017/11/20/yoda-stew|text=Recipe: Yoda Stew|work=Living History in the Star Wars Galaxy: Applying the methods of historic reenacting to the Galaxy Far, Far Away|date=2017-11-20|archivedate=20240123010023}}</ref>
